newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France eyes Delta, Continental cargo links.
newsitem.headline: Air France eyes Delta, Continental cargo links.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it aims to forge close cargo links with U.S. partners Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines to improve its US market share.
Francois Bachelet, executive vice president and chief operating officer, told Reuters he wanted to access the U.S. domestic market better through the U.S. airlines' hubs.
Air France and the two U.S. airlines launched a passenger alliance on April 7 which should lead to code-share flights between France and the U.S. once the two countries have reached a new air pact.
Bachelet said: "One of the main items we have under review is the cargo aspect of the alliances which Air France is building with Continental and Delta.
"This is a huge market where Air France has lots to do to keep up with Lufthansa," he added.
"We have lost market share on the North Atlantic and this is a way to recover."
Air France could feed the Delta hub at Atlanta and the Continental hub at Houston as well as Miami, Bachelet said.
Cooperation would also allow Air France to target Latin American markets such as Caracas by transhipping on to partner flights, he noted.
But Air France already covered Latin America directly with its own freighter flights and in co-operation with Aerolineas Argentinas, he added.
